stories.title: North Wales Crusaders secure RFL future
stories.summary: North Wales Crusaders have secured a place in the Rugby Football League Championship for 2027 despite initially withdrawing their bid for a licence. Crusaders withdrew from the process of bidding for a licence earlier this month after the RFL requested £150,000 in an escrow account to prove financial funding was in place. However, in a statement, the RFL says Crusaders owner Jamie Elkaleh "has revised his business plan and now satisfies all the governing bodies' enquiries". "This is great news for North Wales Crusaders and us, as a sport, as we look forward to the new season," said RFL chief executive Ian Nolan.

stories.title: Canadian Hotel Strikes Gold With Parking Garage Hockey Rink
stories.summary: Youth hockey teams are booking years in advance. Moncton—a city of roughly 100,000—hosts multiple major youth hockey tournaments every winter weekend at its Avenir Centre, just blocks from the Downtown Moncton Garden Inn. (The venue also serves as home ice for the QMJHL's Moncton Wildcats.) The raucous knee-hockey games moved the hotel to build a "youth hockey room"—a ball hockey rink built into the property's underground parking garage. Earlier this week, it announced the return of the mini-rink for a second season. The concept was an instant hit when it debuted last year, but demand has reached a new level.
